name: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 — MODERATE Baseline
description: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Security and Privacy Controls — MODERATE baseline for public-facing web applications. This is a reporting layer: each control maps to parent benchmarks (DISA STIG, CIS NGINX, OWASP ASVS, PCI-DSS) that provide the actual verification. No new checks — results are cross-referenced from parent audit files. This matches how Tenable Nessus maps to NIST through DISA STIG → CCI → NIST 800-53 chains.
honest_disclosure: This is not a standalone check file. Results are derived from DISA STIG V-IDs, CIS NGINX, OWASP ASVS, and PCI-DSS findings. Controls marked 'config_required' require server access. 16/20 controls are assessable from the web perspective via parent benchmarks.

assessability_legend.mapped_from_parents: Verification comes from parent benchmark results in the database
assessability_legend.config_required: Requires server config access — unaudited from web perspective

group_policies.name: AC — Access Control
group_policies.description: Controls limiting system access to authorized users, processes, and devices

items.title: Account Management
items.description: The organization manages information system accounts, including identifying account types, establishing conditions for group membership, and specifying authorized users.
items.remediation: Document and enforce account management policy. Review accounts quarterly.

items.title: Access Enforcement
items.description: The information system enforces approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources.
items.remediation: Enforce access controls on protected resources. Block admin paths.

items.title: Unsuccessful Login Attempts
items.description: The information system enforces a limit of consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user during a defined time period, and automatically locks the account until released by an administrator.
items.remediation: Configure account lockout after 3-5 failed attempts within 15 minutes.

items.title: Session Lock / Session Termination
items.description: The information system prevents further access by initiating a session lock after a defined period of inactivity, and terminates the session after a defined maximum period.
items.remediation: Set session timeout: 5 min (high-risk), 10 min (medium), 20 min (low).

items.title: Permitted Actions Without Identification or Authentication
items.description: The organization identifies user actions that can be performed without identification or authentication.
items.remediation: Document all unauthenticated actions. Restrict admin/debug pages to authenticated users only.

items.title: Data Mining Protection
items.description: The organization employs data mining detection techniques for systems that process, store, or transmit sensitive information to detect data extraction.
items.remediation: Block GPTBot, CCBot, Google-Extended in robots.txt. Add crawl-delay directives.

group_policies.name: CM — Configuration Management
group_policies.description: Controls establishing and maintaining secure baseline configurations

items.title: Configuration Settings
items.description: The organization establishes configuration settings for information technology products employed within the information system.
items.remediation: Document and enforce secure configuration settings. Align with CIS NGINX Benchmark.

items.title: Least Functionality
items.description: The organization configures the information system to provide only essential capabilities and prohibits unnecessary functions.
items.remediation: Remove all unnecessary services, sample code, documentation, and default files. Disable unused modules.

items.title: System Component Inventory
items.description: The organization develops, documents, and maintains an inventory of information system components.
items.remediation: Maintain system component inventory. Publish security.txt per RFC 9116.

group_policies.name: IA — Identification and Authentication
group_policies.description: Controls verifying the identity of users, devices, and processes

items.title: Authenticator Management
items.description: The organization manages information system authenticators by establishing password policies, verifying identity before credential issuance, and protecting authenticator content.
items.remediation: Enforce minimum 12-char passwords with complexity. Rotate every 60-90 days. Enable MFA.

group_policies.name: SC — System and Communications Protection
group_policies.description: Controls protecting system communications and enforcing boundary protections

items.title: Boundary Protection
items.description: The information system monitors and controls communications at the external boundary and at key internal boundaries. Includes WAF, firewall, and security headers.
items.remediation: Deploy WAF. Set CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, and Permissions-Policy headers.

items.title: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity
items.description: The information system protects the confidentiality and integrity of transmitted information. Requires TLS 1.2+ for all data in transit.
items.remediation: Deploy TLS 1.2/1.3 with valid certificate. Redirect HTTP to HTTPS. Deploy NGINX reverse proxy with certbot.

items.title: Cryptographic Protection / Use of Cryptography
items.description: The information system implements cryptographic mechanisms in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, and policies. FIPS 140-2 validated cryptography preferred.
items.remediation: Use FIPS 140-2 validated ciphers. Remove NULL/EXPORT/DES/RC4/3DES. Enable HSTS with 1-year max-age.

items.title: Session Authenticity
items.description: The information system protects the authenticity of communications sessions. Includes secure cookie attributes (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite) and CSRF protections.

covered_by.description: GDPR — cookie consent with session control

items.remediation: Set Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite=Lax/Strict on all cookies. Implement CSRF tokens.

group_policies.name: SI — System and Information Integrity
group_policies.description: Controls maintaining system and data integrity through flaw remediation, malware protection, and error handling

items.title: Flaw Remediation
items.description: The organization identifies, reports, and corrects information system flaws. Includes patch management, CVE tracking, and CDN library version auditing.
items.remediation: Update all CDN libraries to latest versions. Establish patch management cycle. Subscribe to CVE feeds.

items.title: Information Input Validation
items.description: The information system checks the validity of information inputs. Includes CSP, XSS protection, form validation, and content-type enforcement.
items.remediation: Implement CSP with strict script-src. Add SRI hashes to all external scripts. Validate all form inputs.

items.title: Error Handling
items.description: The information system generates error messages that provide information necessary for corrective actions without revealing information that could be exploited by adversaries.

covered_by.description: OWASP 7.1.1 — no debug leakage in HTML

items.remediation: Create custom 40x/50x error pages. Remove stack traces, file paths, and debug info from production pages.

group_policies.name: RA — Risk Assessment
group_policies.description: Controls for assessing organizational risk through vulnerability scanning and analysis

items.title: Vulnerability Scanning
items.description: The organization scans for vulnerabilities in the information system and hosted applications periodically and when new vulnerabilities are identified.
items.remediation: Conduct quarterly vulnerability scans. Use authenticated scanning for internal systems. Remediate critical findings within 30 days.

group_policies.name: AU — Audit and Accountability
group_policies.description: Controls for audit logging, monitoring, and non-repudiation

items.title: Event Logging / Audit Events
items.description: The organization determines that the information system is capable of auditing specific events. Includes access logs, error logs, and security event logging.
items.remediation: Enable web server access and error logging. Configure log format to include client IP, timestamp, request method, URI, status, and user agent.

group_policies.name: CP — Contingency Planning
group_policies.description: Controls for business continuity, disaster recovery, and backup management

items.title: System Backup / Information System Backup
items.description: The organization conducts backups of user-level and system-level information and protects backup information.
items.remediation: Implement automated daily backups. Store backups offsite. Test restoration quarterly.
